This is direct industry-level evidence that the dry-bulk freight cycle is active.

primary_cause: Drewry's 3 Sep 2026 WCI shows the global benchmark holding at USD 4,465/FEU, with Transpacific rates rising, resilient demand, and carriers reducing capacity through additional blank sailings. The cycle is active but geographically mixed rather than uniformly accelerating.
counter_evidence: Asia-Europe spot rates weakened in the same weekly update, with Shanghai-Genoa down 10% and Shanghai-Rotterdam down 5%, so the signal is not broad-based acceleration.
source_summary: Drewry World Container Index 2026-09-03: WCI stable at $4,465/40ft; Shanghai-LA +5%, Shanghai-NY +3%; six blank sailings announced, resilient demand and capacity management expected to keep rates stable. https://www.drewry.co.uk/supply-chain-advisors/supply-chain-expertise/world-container-index-assessed-by-drewry/freight-cost-benchmarking

primary_cause: Current evidence confirms major nuclear buildout ambitions, but I did not find sufficiently direct evidence that nuclear-specific projects are presently the causal driver of second-order transformer, switchgear, or transmission-equipment demand. Broad grid tightness and broad electrification cannot be substituted for this narrow driver.
source_summary: Reuters 2026-09-02 reports India's target to expand nuclear capacity to 100 GW by 2047 with roughly $210B investment, confirming nuclear buildout activity but not the specific second-order grid-equipment causal edge. https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/india-urged-review-green-finance-rules-build-workforce-nuclear-expansion-2026-09-02/

primary_cause: Multiple independent company and industry sources show broad, current demand for electrical power-management equipment and data-center power infrastructure: Eaton reports sharply higher electrical orders and backlog, Schneider reports very high data-center demand and record backlog, and Reuters documents surging demand for power infrastructure and cooling. This is sufficient to classify the power-electronics/equipment capex cycle as active.
counter_evidence: A material counter-risk is speculative or duplicated data-center interconnection demand ('ghost demand'), which can overstate eventual realized grid capex in some U.S. regions.
source_summary: Eaton Q2 2026: Electrical Americas rolling orders +41%, Electrical Global +33%, strong backlog, data centers a key growth driver. https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-second-quarter-2026-results.html | Schneider Electric H1 2026: data-center demand remained very high; Energy Management broad-based growth; record backlog. https://www.se.com/ww/en/about-us/investor-relations/financial-results/ | Reuters 2026-09-01: power and cooling firms report surging backlogs and production expansion amid AI data-center buildout. https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/not-just-nvidia-these-power-cooling-firms-are-riding-trillion-dollar-data-centre-2026-09-01/

primary_cause: The exact shipment cycle is directly supported by industry shipment forecasts and broad OEM/ODM demand evidence. TrendForce raised 2026 AI-server shipment growth to nearly 31% YoY and continues to report strong CSP capex, GPU-rack orders, and ODM shipment momentum; Dell and HPE simultaneously report exceptional AI-server orders/backlog and demand exceeding supply.
counter_evidence: Supply constraints in memory, NAND, CPUs and drives may limit near-term fulfillment, but they currently constrain supply rather than contradict demand or shipment-cycle strength.
